the_two_hypotheses.H-texture: whatever latched the stack into the dim mode acted on TEXTURED-BODY rendering (the shared s_texture content, its upload, its residency). §11.159(a) established that the star channel's pixels come from HipStarMgr::color_table (zone_array.cpp), not from any texture the Moon uses.
the_two_hypotheses.H-global: the dim mode was a global output transform (gamma / colour space / swapchain format / compositor-side conversion), which would darken EVERY drawn pixel including stars.

P7_star_channel_across_the_dim_boundary.H-texture predicts: today's sky.png is photometrically indistinguishable from the 2026-08-29 ones — ideally an exact md5 match with one of the two committed classes, at worst a difference inside §11.159(k)(4)'s measured A/A floor (374 px of 4194304 at max channel delta 3/255)
P7_star_channel_across_the_dim_boundary.H-global predicts: the 2026-08-29 star frames are systematically darker than today's on the lit pixels — a mean-luma ratio far from 1.0 and a difference vastly outside the A/A floor
P7_star_channel_across_the_dim_boundary.prior_evidence_favouring_H-texture: both render paths were dim (§11.172(f)) and they share one s_texture entry; the app logs were clean; 0 `Can't upload` in every run
P7_star_channel_across_the_dim_boundary.prior_evidence_favouring_H-global: BOTH paths dim is also what a global transform looks like, and §11.167's dark-patch signature was non-tone-curve (r2 0.408) which a simple gamma would not produce
P7_star_channel_across_the_dim_boundary.fails_if: either hypothesis's prediction lands and it is NOT the one the ledger currently leans on — recorded as it comes, at the node
P7_star_channel_across_the_dim_boundary.bound_stated_in_advance: the star field is a SPARSE scene; a dimming of a few dark pixels could hide inside the frame statistics. The metric is therefore taken on the LIT pixels (L > 8) and on the max channel delta, not on the whole-frame mean, and the lit-pixel COUNT is reported too — a global darkening moves pixels across the L>8 threshold and that count is the sensitive member.
